analysis: The PR contains only documentation and a changelog; no Swift or Go code is in the batch. The changelog describes provider code changes (endpoint resumption, logout drain and revoke, token-issuer binding, resume frame limits) that are not visible here, so they were not reviewed. attestation.md head line 112 adopts platform-revision semantics. Basic serving no longer requires a verified recurring receipt or risk metric, and last-known policy may be retained for an established identity. This contradicts the canonical header notes and T-055/T-057, which require a fresh verified risk receipt for every grant. The changelog claims the threat model was aligned, but threat-model.yaml is not in the diff. provider.md head lines 66-77 and attestation.md describe a new same-process endpoint-resumption custody response. It is origin-bound and has no Apple operation, but it feeds platform-side connection-bound authorization (TB-011, A-016, T-053). Next passes should check the responder source (ProviderLoop+Serve.swift, CoordinatorClient.connectAndRun) and the platform side for nonce reuse, replay across sockets, and frame-limit enforcement. They should also check that logout token revocation fails closed and that the coordinator revocation URL has an issuer check.

findings.detail: The head text replaces the statement that a serving grant needs a verified current risk receipt with the platform-revision semantics. Under those semantics, missing recurring receipt/risk evidence neither blocks otherwise qualified basic serving nor triggers further assertions. It also allows an 'established exact identity' to retain last-known policy when administrative reads fail, within ceilings. The canonical threat model, including its header notes on first-grant recovery, states that every serving grant needs a fresh verified risk receipt. T-055 and T-057 rely on that. The changelog says the retained threat model is aligned, but no threat-model file is in this change. A provider whose receipt or risk evidence is absent or unverified can now serve, so the 'receipt as a gate' mitigation is no longer a valid assumption. Revocation and administrative-read staleness are bounded only by ceilings the PR does not quantify. Fix: update threat-model.yaml (T-053, T-055, T-057, TB-011) in this PR with the new gating, the receipt-monitoring split and the stale-policy ceilings. Mark the document as platform-only, not this snapshot's behavior.
findings.title: Docs weaken the receipt-required serving grant while the threat model still asserts it

findings.detail: The provider now answers a protocol-1 endpoint-resumption challenge synchronously in CoordinatorClient with the in-memory X25519 key and a fresh per-socket nonce. It bypasses ProviderLoop and its Apple operation admission. The documentation says a platform can use this response with retained evidence on a new connection without a fresh Apple assertion. That is a new input to connection-bound serving authorization (A-016, TB-011), and it relies on process-key custody. A-003 and T-011 say the key is readable by the operator. The responder's code is not in this batch, so its replay and nonce binding cannot be verified here. The threat model does not mention this path. Fix: add a threat entry and mitigation for resumption covering nonce freshness and origin binding, original proof deadlines, and revocation checks on resumed connections. The platform side must also verify the custody proof against the current endpoint binding.
findings.title: New endpoint-resumption custody path is not covered by the threat model
